False-event accounting of a normal-mode result: p- and q-values, expected false calls and events

Source: R/event_fdr.R
event_fdr.Rd

Output only: no call, threshold, score or existing column changes. The q column is descriptive: it is not a false discovery rate and must not be used as a filter (see q-value).

Usage

event_fdr(
  obj,
  tail = c("exponential", "none"),
  tail_n = 50,
  resolve_gains = NULL,
  gain_min_dl = NULL,
  gain_gate = NULL,
  gain_gate_q = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05
)

Arguments

obj

normal-mode scphasedcn with scores (caller_normal(); call_scn() with keep_scores)

tail

"exponential" (tail model beyond the top tail_n null scores) or "none" (the conformal p-value only)

tail_n

null scores above the tail anchor (per calibration group)

resolve_gains, gain_min_dl

the gain gate of the run (caller_normal() arguments; default the run's recorded params$normal, else the caller_normal() defaults)

gain_gate, gain_gate_q

the gain depth gate of the run ("dl" or "z", caller_normal(); default the run's recorded params$normal, else "z" when the calls carry the gate columns of resolve_nested() (gate_thr), else "dl"; gain_gate_q default 0.95). The "z" gate uses the run's depth null (null_fit$tpar)

alpha

q-value level of the descriptive summary count (n_q_below in info; not a false discovery rate)

Value

list: calls (the result's calls with p, q (descriptive, not a false discovery rate), null_borrowed on the tested per-cell rows, NA elsewhere), events (the result's events with null_cell, p, q (of the top region) and null_borrowed; NA for pool events), expected_false (class, state, chrom_group, null_borrowed, n_rows, n_tested, n_called, n_events, n_null, n_null_called, n_null_events, null_per_1000, expected_false_calls (+ _lo, _hi), expected_false_events (+ _lo, _hi), false_frac_calls, false_frac_events), groups (per calibration group: class, stratum, n_null, p_floor = 1 / (n + 1), borrowed) and info (m, tail, tail_n, alpha, the gain gate)

Details

Tested rows. The per-cell rows of the classes that are reportable per cell (call_policy(): chromosomes, arms, 50 Mb tiles, named events) with a threshold, plus the 20 Mb rows that resolve_nested() promoted to reportable. Each row is a hypothesis "this cell-region is null". Its test statistic is the score of a reportable call, s' = s_comb when the row would be reportable if called (its best state is reportable for its class, and a chromosome / event gain passes the depth gate of the run's resolve_nested(): dl_gain > gain_min_dl with gain_gate = "dl", z above its null-quantile threshold with the opt-in gain_gate = "z"; a called row uses its final reportable flag, so a gain that lost to a nested loss or failed the gate counts as not reportable and a promoted row as reportable), else -Inf. A gain the gate removes thus stays in the tested family with p = 1, and the null rows are scored by the same rule, so the gate is applied to the calls, their p-values and the expected-false accounting alike.

p-value. Against the null rows (is_null) of the row's threshold group (class x depth stratum, x vote stratum with calib = "votes", with the same pooled fallback as budget_thresholds()) in the cross-validation folds the row's threshold was trained on (all folds but its own): p = (1 + #{null s' >= s'}) / (n + 1) (a conformal p-value; p = 1 for s' = -Inf). With n null rows p cannot go below 1 / (n + 1) (the resolution limit; ~1e-4 to 1e-5 per group on real data), and reportable null calls are rare, so the empirical p of every strong call sits at that floor. Under BH with m tests a single event then cannot reach a q below about m / (n + 1), which is several times 1 (m is larger than n: all cells x all tested rows against the null rows of one class x stratum), and the q of a strong event depends only on how many other events are as strong. tail = "exponential" (default) therefore extends the p-value beyond the anchor u, the (tail_n + 1)-th largest null s_comb of the group (whatever the state), with an exponential tail fitted to the top tail_n null scores (peaks over threshold; beta = their mean excess over u, the maximum-likelihood fit) times the reportable share of that tail: p = (a + 1) / (n + 1) exp(-(s' - u) / beta), a = reportable rows among the top tail_n; the two pieces meet at u. The exponential tail is conservative when the null is correctly specified and light-tailed (near-Gaussian allelic log-likelihood ratios, the bounded Student-t depth term); it is a model, not a guarantee against artefacts the null cells do not carry.

Relative to the selected null. The p-values, and the tail beyond the largest null scores, are relative to the selected null cells (select_null_cells()). The selection removes the cells with the heaviest tails (e.g. cells with a higher allelic overdispersion than modelled), so for cells like those the p-values are too small, and the tail model extrapolates a truncated distribution: in such a sample many rows can reach a small q with the exponential tail and none with tail = "none". Compare the two when the null is in doubt. Rows on chromosomes without null rows (chrX, whose rows are never null rows in normal mode) are compared with the autosomal null of their class x stratum, as their thresholds are (null_borrowed = TRUE).

Named events. A class without null rows (named event regions) takes the thresholds of its sd_class (budget_thresholds()), and its p-values are calibrated on the same rows: the null rows of the sd_class group (and folds) its threshold was trained on, each scored as an event row would be (s_comb when its best state is reportable for an event and a gain passes the depth gate, else -Inf; the sd_class's own calling policy differs, e.g. arm gains are not reportable per cell). null_borrowed = TRUE; in groups such a group has the sd_class as class and borrowed = TRUE. The p-values are as good as the assumption behind the borrowed thresholds: that the event's scores under the null look like those of its sd_class (similar size and allele votes).

q-value. Benjamini-Hochberg over all tested rows (m = every tested row, called or not; rows with s' = -Inf have p = 1 and count in m). Within a class x stratum and fold, q is monotone in the score. q is a descriptive column: it is not a false discovery rate and must not be used as a filter. It is too small in two independent ways. (1) The unit is the row, not the event: one real event typically rejects several nested rows (its chromosome, arms, tiles), which loosens the cut-off for single-row false events, so the false share among events (an event carries the q of its top region) with q below a cut can be well above the cut (in a simulation with 300 planted chromosome losses in 3,000 cells, 12 % of the events with q < 0.05 were false). (2) The p-values are relative to the selected null cells and the default tail is fitted to them (see above; on a simulated null in which 10 % of the cells had a higher allelic overdispersion, 28 events reached q < 0.05, all false, and none with tail = "none"). No event-level q-value is computed.

Expected false calls and events (expected_false, one row per class x state x chromosome group A (autosomes) / X / Y): per depth stratum, the realised rate of reportable calls of that state among the null rows of the class (fold-cross-validated thresholds, the calling policy and the gain gate applied, as for every cell), times the number of per-cell rows of the class, summed over the strata (expected_false_calls); the same with the null cells' events whose top region is a null row of that class (expected_false_events, so nested calls count once). Every row of the class counts as a null hypothesis (no estimate of the null fraction), and the null rate is measured on cells selected for having no chromosome / arm call at a stricter threshold (select_null_cells()), whose own rows are cleaner than those of an unselected normal cell: both estimates are lower bounds of the false load. chrX rows borrow the autosomal rate (null_borrowed), which ignores X-inactivation driven allelic imbalance. A class without null rows (named events) takes the rate of its sd_class's null rows called as event rows (per sd_class x stratum; that call rate also stands for its events). null_selection_check() measures how much the selection lowers the rate.
